     9	/-!
    10	# The universal divisor rank-one open contract
    11	
    12	The genus divisor representer is unconditional, while the rank-one restriction still needs a
    13	family-level open-locus producer.  This file separates those two facts.  The predicate below is
    14	the inverse image of `PicRankOneOpen` along the represented universal Abel map.  A
    15	`DivRankOneOpenData` witness identifies that predicate with the range of one actual open of the
    16	representer; only after that witness is supplied do we define the open subscheme.
    17	
    18	This shape prevents a logical `Subfunctor` from being silently reinterpreted as a scheme.  It also
    19	gives the canonical inverse lane a stable contract: it consumes the witness equality and can use
    20	the resulting open inclusion and all of its pullbacks without choosing a generator.
    21	-/
    22	
    23	set_option autoImplicit false
    24	set_option maxSynthPendingDepth 3
    25	
    26	universe u
    27	
    28	open CategoryTheory Limits Opposite
    29	
    30	namespace AlgebraicGeometry
    31	
    32	variable {k : Type u} [Field k] {C : Over (Spec (.of k))}
    33	variable [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom]
    34	  [GeometricallyIrreducible C.hom]
    35	variable (pi : C.left ⟶ P1 k) [IsFinite pi]
    36	
    37	noncomputable section
    38	
    39	/-- The universal genus-divisor predicate whose Abel class lies in `PicRankOneOpen`. -/
    40	def divRankOneUniversalPredicate :
    41	    Subfunctor (yoneda.obj (divRepAffGenusScheme C)) :=
    42	  divRankOnePresentationPreimageRepresenter pi
    43	
    44	/-- The Yoneda map induced by the inclusion of an open of an object in the slice.  Naming this
    45	map is useful to consumers which need the actual factorisation through the open, rather than only
    46	the proposition that a point lies in its range. -/
    47	def openSubfunctorMap (D : Over (Spec (.of k))) (U : D.left.Opens) :
    48	    yoneda.obj (Over.mk (U.ι ≫ D.hom)) ⟶ yoneda.obj D :=
    49	  yoneda.map (Over.homMk (U := Over.mk (U.ι ≫ D.hom)) U.ι)
    50	
    51	/-- The subfunctor represented by an open `U` of an object `D` in the slice over `Spec k`.
    52	
    53	Its values are precisely morphisms which factor through the open immersion `U.ι`; using the
    54	Yoneda range keeps this definition independent of any chosen affine presentation of `U`. -/
    55	def openSubfunctor (D : Over (Spec (.of k))) (U : D.left.Opens) :
    56	    Subfunctor (yoneda.obj D) :=
    57	  Subfunctor.range (openSubfunctorMap D U)
    58	
    59	/-- Unpack range membership into the actual source point and its equality in the ambient Yoneda
    60	functor.  This is the pointwise factorisation API used by inverse constructions. -/
    61	theorem openSubfunctor_mem_iff
    62	    (D : Over (Spec (.of k))) (U : D.left.Opens)
    63	    {T : (Over (Spec (.of k)))ᵒᵖ}
    64	    (x : (yoneda.obj D).obj T) :
    65	    x ∈ (openSubfunctor D U).obj T ↔
    66	      ∃ y : (yoneda.obj (Over.mk (U.ι ≫ D.hom))).obj T,
    67	        (openSubfunctorMap D U).app T y = x := by
    68	  rfl
    69	
    70	/-- An explicit geometric certificate for the universal rank-one predicate.
    71	
    72	The equality is the missing family-level producer/gluing statement: it identifies the logical
    73	preimage with an actual open of the canonical genus representer.  No default or top-open witness
    74	is manufactured here. -/
    75	structure DivRankOneOpenData (pi : C.left ⟶ P1 k) [IsFinite pi] where
    76	  carrier : (divRepAffGenusScheme C).left.Opens
    77	  carrier_eq :
    78	    openSubfunctor (divRepAffGenusScheme C) carrier =
    79	      divRankOneUniversalPredicate pi
    80	
    81	/-- The open subscheme supplied by a `DivRankOneOpenData` witness. -/
    82	def DivRankOneOpen (h : DivRankOneOpenData (C := C) pi) : Scheme :=
    83	  h.carrier.toScheme
    84	
    85	/-- The canonical open immersion into the genus divisor representer. -/
    86	def divRankOneOpenMap (h : DivRankOneOpenData (C := C) pi) :
    87	    DivRankOneOpen pi h ⟶ (divRepAffGenusScheme C).left :=
    88	  h.carrier.ι
    89	
    90	theorem divRankOneOpen_isOpenImmersion
    91	    (h : DivRankOneOpenData (C := C) pi) :
    92	    IsOpenImmersion (divRankOneOpenMap pi h) := by
    93	  change IsOpenImmersion h.carrier.ι
    94	  infer_instance
    95	
    96	/-- The open represented object, retained in the slice over `Spec k` for consumers of the affine
    97	divisor functor. -/
    98	def divRankOneOpenOver (h : DivRankOneOpenData (C := C) pi) :
    99	    Over (Spec (.of k)) :=
   100	  Over.mk (divRankOneOpenMap pi h ≫ (divRepAffGenusScheme C).hom)
   101	
   102	/-- The inclusion of the certified open, as a morphism in the slice over `Spec k`.
   103	
   104	This is the map whose Yoneda action is consumed by the canonical rank-one Abel inverse.  Naming
   105	it separately keeps consumers independent of the implementation spelling of `divRankOneOpenOver`.
   106	-/
   107	def divRankOneOpenOverMap (h : DivRankOneOpenData (C := C) pi) :
   108	    divRankOneOpenOver pi h ⟶ divRepAffGenusScheme C :=
   109	  Over.homMk (divRankOneOpenMap pi h)
   110	
   111	/-- Pull back the certified rank-one open along an arbitrary slice morphism. -/
   112	def divRankOneOpenPullback
   113	    (h : DivRankOneOpenData (C := C) pi)
   114	    {T : Over (Spec (.of k))} (q : T ⟶ divRepAffGenusScheme C) : T.left.Opens :=
   115	  q.left ⁻¹ᵁ h.carrier
   116	
   117	theorem divRankOneOpenPullback_isOpenImmersion
   118	    (h : DivRankOneOpenData (C := C) pi)
   119	    {T : Over (Spec (.of k))} (q : T ⟶ divRepAffGenusScheme C) :
   120	    IsOpenImmersion (divRankOneOpenPullback pi h q).ι := by
   121	  infer_instance
   122	
   123	/-- Pointwise form of arbitrary base-change compatibility for the certified open. -/
   124	theorem mem_divRankOneOpenPullback_iff
   125	    (h : DivRankOneOpenData (C := C) pi)
   126	    {T : Over (Spec (.of k))} (q : T ⟶ divRepAffGenusScheme C)
   127	    (x : T.left) :
   128	    x ∈ divRankOneOpenPullback pi h q ↔ q.left.base x ∈ h.carrier := by
   129	  rfl
   130	
   131	/-- The universal predicate is exactly the represented preimage used by the Abel restriction. -/
   132	theorem divRankOneUniversalPredicate_eq_preimage :
   133	    divRankOneUniversalPredicate pi = divRankOnePresentationPreimageRepresenter pi :=
   134	  rfl
   135	
   136	/-- The certified open carrier has the universal rank-one predicate as its Yoneda range. -/
   137	theorem divRankOneOpen_carrier_eq
   138	    (h : DivRankOneOpenData (C := C) pi) :
   139	    openSubfunctor (divRepAffGenusScheme C) h.carrier =
   140	      divRankOneUniversalPredicate pi :=
   141	  h.carrier_eq
   142	
   143	/-- Pointwise form of the witness equality, exposing the exact contract consumed by an inverse.
   144	
   145	The right-hand side is the range of the open immersion, so a consumer can use this theorem to
   146	replace a rank-one predicate proof by a factorisation through `DivRankOneOpen pi h`. -/
   147	theorem divRankOneOpen_mem_iff
   148	    (h : DivRankOneOpenData (C := C) pi)
   149	    {T : (Over (Spec (.of k)))ᵒᵖ}
   150	    (x : (yoneda.obj (divRepAffGenusScheme C)).obj T) :
   151	    x ∈ (divRankOneUniversalPredicate pi).obj T ↔
   152	      x ∈ (openSubfunctor (divRepAffGenusScheme C) h.carrier).obj T := by
   153	  rw [h.carrier_eq]
   154	
   155	/-- A point of the universal rank-one predicate factors through the certified open immersion.
   156	
   157	Unlike a bare range-membership proof, the conclusion exposes the source point and the equality
   158	of its image with the given divisor point, which is the exact data needed by a canonical inverse. -/
   159	theorem divRankOneOpen_mem_iff_factorization
   160	    (h : DivRankOneOpenData (C := C) pi)
   161	    {T : (Over (Spec (.of k)))ᵒᵖ}
   162	    (x : (yoneda.obj (divRepAffGenusScheme C)).obj T) :
   163	    x ∈ (divRankOneUniversalPredicate pi).obj T ↔
   164	      ∃ y : (yoneda.obj (Over.mk
   165	          (h.carrier.ι ≫ (divRepAffGenusScheme C).hom))).obj T,
   166	        (openSubfunctorMap (divRepAffGenusScheme C) h.carrier).app T y = x := by
   167	  rw [divRankOneOpen_mem_iff pi h x, openSubfunctor_mem_iff]
   168	
   169	/-- The same factorisation contract with the named open object and slice inclusion.
   170	
   171	The source in the preceding theorem is definitionally the slice object
   172	`divRankOneOpenOver pi h`; this corollary gives the stable public names expected by inverse
   173	consumers. -/
   174	theorem divRankOneOpen_mem_iff_factorization_over
   175	    (h : DivRankOneOpenData (C := C) pi)
   176	    {T : (Over (Spec (.of k)))ᵒᵖ}
   177	    (x : (yoneda.obj (divRepAffGenusScheme C)).obj T) :
   178	    x ∈ (divRankOneUniversalPredicate pi).obj T ↔
   179	      ∃ y : (yoneda.obj (divRankOneOpenOver pi h)).obj T,
   180	        (yoneda.map (divRankOneOpenOverMap pi h)).app T y = x := by
   181	  rw [divRankOneOpen_mem_iff_factorization pi h x]
   182	  rfl
   183	
   184	/-- A point in the certified open carrier is a point of the universal rank-one predicate. -/
   185	theorem divRankOneOpen_mem_of_carrier
   186	    (h : DivRankOneOpenData (C := C) pi)
   187	    {T : (Over (Spec (.of k)))ᵒᵖ}
   188	    {x : (yoneda.obj (divRepAffGenusScheme C)).obj T}
   189	    (hx : x ∈ (openSubfunctor (divRepAffGenusScheme C) h.carrier).obj T) :
   190	    x ∈ (divRankOneUniversalPredicate pi).obj T := by
   191	  exact (divRankOneOpen_mem_iff pi h x).mpr hx
   192	
   193	/- The logical rank-one predicate remains stable under arbitrary pullback, independently of the
   194	   geometric witness used to represent it by an open. -/
   195	theorem divRankOneOpen_baseChange_mem
   196	    {T T' : (Over (Spec (.of k)))ᵒᵖ}
   197	    (f : T ⟶ T')
   198	    {x : (yoneda.obj (divRepAffGenusScheme C)).obj T}
   199	    (hx : x ∈ (divRankOneUniversalPredicate pi).obj T) :
   200	    (yoneda.obj (divRepAffGenusScheme C)).map f x ∈
   201	      (divRankOneUniversalPredicate pi).obj T' :=
   202	  (divRankOneUniversalPredicate pi).map f hx
   203	
   204	end
   205	
   206	end AlgebraicGeometry

    16	/-!
    17	# The local-presentation contract for the rank-one Picard locus
    18	
    19	An element of `picDegLayerFunctor` is an etale-plus class, not a chosen line bundle.  The
    20	rank-one route therefore needs an explicit local presentation before it can use the evaluation
    21	map of a line bundle.  `PicRankOneLocalPresentation` records that presentation on an affine
    22	test and ties every piece of data to the input class:
    23	
    24	* a descent-class representative whose plus class is the affine collapse of the input;
    25	* a cocycle datum presenting that same relative Picard class;
    26	* a locally free rank-one `Scheme.Modules` object whose base-ring sheaf is the datum's sheaf;
    27	* invertibility of the canonical native pushforward base-change mate on every cartesian square;
    28	* the cohomological rank-one outputs used by the evaluation construction.
    29	
    30	No existence, openness, or representability assertion is made here.  The first canonical
    31	consumer is `PicRankOneLocalPresentation.evaluation`, the pullback-pushforward counit.
    32	The method `PicRankOneLocalPresentation.h0BaseChange` derives arbitrary affine base change
    33	from the same presentation's `H^1`-vanishing field.  The section bridge at the end identifies
    34	datum `H^0` with native global sections and proves, by the adjunction triangle identity, that

    48	namespace AlgebraicGeometry

    55	  [GeometricallyIrreducible C.hom]
    56	variable {A : Type u} [CommRing A] [Algebra k A]
    57	variable (pi : C.left ⟶ P1 k) [IsFinite pi]

    59	/-- A rank-one presentation of a genus-degree plus class on an affine test.
    60

   172	        ((Scheme.Modules.pushforward
   173	          (relCurve C P.cover.Carrier ↘ Spec (.of P.cover.Carrier))).obj P.module) ≅
   174	      (Scheme.Modules.pushforward f' ⋙ Scheme.Modules.pullback f').obj

   177	    Scheme.Modules.pullbackCongr sq.w.symm ≪≫
   178	    (Scheme.Modules.pullbackComp g'
   179	      (relCurve C P.cover.Carrier ↘ Spec (.of P.cover.Carrier))).symm).app
   180	        ((Scheme.Modules.pushforward
   181	          (relCurve C P.cover.Carrier ↘ Spec (.of P.cover.Carrier))).obj P.module)).symm) ≪≫
   182	    (Scheme.Modules.pullback f').mapIso (P.nativeBaseChangeIso g f' g' sq)

   184	/-- Under the source identification, evaluation after base change is the pullback of the
   185	presentation's original evaluation counit. -/
   186	theorem evaluationSourceBaseChangeIso_hom_evaluation

   383	/-- Nonvanishing on every residue-field fibre of `D(f)` survives passage from the
   384	corresponding prime of the original ring to the residue field of a prime of `A_f`.

   387	residue-field maps.  Keeping this as a private module lemma prevents the rank-one

   390	    {A Q : Type u} [CommRing A] [AddCommGroup Q] [Module A Q]
   391	    (f : A) (y : Q)
   392	    (hy : ∀ p : PrimeSpectrum A, f ∉ p.asIdeal →
   393	      (y ⊗ₜ (1 : p.asIdeal.ResidueField) :
   394	        Q ⊗[A] p.asIdeal.ResidueField) ≠ 0)
   395	    (q : PrimeSpectrum (Localization.Away f)) :
   396	    ((1 : q.asIdeal.ResidueField) ⊗ₜ[A] y :
   397	      q.asIdeal.ResidueField ⊗[A] Q) ≠ 0 := by
   398	  let p : PrimeSpectrum A :=
   399	    PrimeSpectrum.comap (algebraMap A (Localization.Away f)) q
   400	  have hfp : f ∉ p.asIdeal := by
   401	    intro hf
   402	    refine q.isPrime.ne_top (Ideal.eq_top_of_isUnit_mem q.asIdeal
   403	      (Ideal.mem_comap.mp hf) ?_)
   404	    exact IsLocalization.Away.algebraMap_isUnit f
   405	  have hp : ((1 : p.asIdeal.ResidueField) ⊗ₜ[A] y :
   406	      p.asIdeal.ResidueField ⊗[A] Q) ≠ 0 := by
   407	    have h := (TensorProduct.comm A Q p.asIdeal.ResidueField).map_ne_zero_iff.mpr
   408	      (hy p hfp)
   409	    simpa only [TensorProduct.comm_tmul] using h
   410	  have hcom : p.asIdeal =
   411	      q.asIdeal.comap (algebraMap A (Localization.Away f)) := rfl
   412	  let rho : p.asIdeal.ResidueField →ₐ[A] q.asIdeal.ResidueField :=
   413	    Ideal.ResidueField.mapₐ p.asIdeal q.asIdeal
   414	      (Algebra.ofId A (Localization.Away f)) hcom
   415	  have hrho : Function.Bijective rho :=
   416	    (RingHom.surjectiveOnStalks_of_isLocalization (Submonoid.powers f)
   417	      (Localization.Away f)).residueFieldMap_bijective
   418	        p.asIdeal q.asIdeal hcom
   419	  let e : p.asIdeal.ResidueField ≃ₗ[A] q.asIdeal.ResidueField :=
   420	    LinearEquiv.ofBijective rho.toLinearMap hrho
   421	  have he := (e.rTensor Q).map_ne_zero_iff.mpr hp
   422	  simpa only [LinearEquiv.rTensor_tmul, e, LinearEquiv.ofBijective_apply,
   423	    AlgHom.toLinearMap_apply, map_one] using he

   537	    Subsingleton (datumPair (P.datum.baseChange B)).H1 :=
   538	  (subsingleton_datumPair_h1_iff (P.datum.baseChange B)).mpr
   539	    (P.datum.datum_subsingleton_h1_baseChange B
   540	      ((subsingleton_datumPair_h1_iff P.datum).mpr P.h1_vanishing))
   541	
   542	/-- The local-away generator supplied over the presentation ring gives the exact
   543	fibrewise-nonvanishing hypothesis required by the divisor construction after localizing.
   544	
   545	This is the missing consumer bridge between the finite-projective generator theorem and
   546	`sectionLocalEquationsOfDatumSectionBaseChange`.  It compares residue fields across the
   547	localization, cancels the iterated tensor product, and then uses the presentation's
   548	canonical `H⁰` base-change equivalence. -/
   549	theorem sectionsMapTop_datumSectionBaseChange_away_ne_zero
   550	    (P : PicRankOneLocalPresentation pi lam)
   551	    (f : P.cover.Carrier)
   552	    (y : Sheaf.HModule P.datum.sheaf 0)
   553	    (hy : ∀ p : PrimeSpectrum P.cover.Carrier, f ∉ p.asIdeal →
   554	      (y ⊗ₜ (1 : p.asIdeal.ResidueField) :
   555	        Sheaf.HModule P.datum.sheaf 0 ⊗[P.cover.Carrier]
   556	          p.asIdeal.ResidueField) ≠ 0)
   557	    (q : PrimeSpectrum (Localization.Away f)) :
   558	    (P.datum.baseChange (Localization.Away f)).sectionsMapTop
   559	      q.asIdeal.ResidueField
   560	      (P.datumSectionBaseChange (Localization.Away f) y) ≠ 0 := by
   561	  let B := Localization.Away f
   562	  let K := q.asIdeal.ResidueField
   563	  have hiter : ((1 : K) ⊗ₜ[B]
   564	      ((1 : B) ⊗ₜ[P.cover.Carrier] y) :
   565	      K ⊗[B] (B ⊗[P.cover.Carrier]
   566	        Sheaf.HModule P.datum.sheaf 0)) ≠ 0 :=
   567	    away_one_tmul_one_tmul_ne_zero f y hy q
   568	  have hyB : ((1 : K) ⊗ₜ[B]
   569	      (P.h0BaseChange B ((1 : B) ⊗ₜ[P.cover.Carrier] y)) :
   570	      K ⊗[B] Sheaf.HModule (P.datum.baseChange B).sheaf 0) ≠ 0 :=
   571	    P.h0BaseChange_one_tmul_ne_zero B K y hiter
   572	  have hH1 : Subsingleton (datumPair (P.datum.baseChange B)).H1 :=
   573	    P.datumPair_h1_baseChange B
   574	  let yB : Sheaf.HModule (P.datum.baseChange B).sheaf 0 :=
   575	    P.h0BaseChange B ((1 : B) ⊗ₜ[P.cover.Carrier] y)
   576	  change (P.datum.baseChange B).sectionsMapTop K
   577	    (Sheaf.HModule.linearEquiv₀
   578	      (Opens.grothendieckTopology ((relCurve C B : Scheme.{u}) : TopCat))
   579	      isTerminalTop (P.datum.baseChange B).sheaf yB) ≠ 0
   580	  exact sectionsMapTop_ne_zero_of_one_tmul_ne_zero
   581	    (P.datum.baseChange B) hH1 yB hyB
   582	
   583	/-- A rank-one presentation has a tied local-away evaluation generator.
   584	
   585	The rank-one field of `P` makes every residue-field fibre of its `H⁰` module nontrivial.
   586	The projective-module generator lemma therefore supplies a single basic open `D(f)` and
   587	one datum section `y` which stays nonzero on every residue fibre over that open.  The same
   588	`y` is transported to a native global section and its unit-lift through the evaluation
   589	counit; the final conjunct records that counit identity explicitly so the future
   590	`divisorOfRankOne` construction consumes this witness rather than an unrelated section.
   591	-/
   592	theorem exists_baseOpen_evaluation_generator
   593	    (P : PicRankOneLocalPresentation pi lam)
   594	    (p : PrimeSpectrum P.cover.Carrier) :
   595	    ∃ f : P.cover.Carrier, f ∉ p.asIdeal ∧
   596	      ∃ y : Sheaf.HModule P.datum.sheaf 0,
   597	        (∀ q : PrimeSpectrum P.cover.Carrier, f ∉ q.asIdeal →
   598	          (y ⊗ₜ (1 : q.asIdeal.ResidueField) :
   599	            Sheaf.HModule P.datum.sheaf 0 ⊗[P.cover.Carrier]
   600	              q.asIdeal.ResidueField) ≠ 0) ∧
   601	        (Scheme.Modules.Hom.app P.evaluation
   602	          ((relCurve C P.cover.Carrier ↘ Spec (.of P.cover.Carrier)) ⁻¹ᵁ
   603	            (⊤ : (Spec (.of P.cover.Carrier)).Opens))).hom
   604	          (P.evaluationLiftOfH0 y) = P.pushforwardSectionOfH0 y := by
   605	  let Q := Sheaf.HModule P.datum.sheaf 0
   606	  letI : Module.Finite P.cover.Carrier Q := P.h0_finite
   607	  letI : Module.Projective P.cover.Carrier Q := P.h0_projective
   608	  have hfr : Module.finrank p.asIdeal.ResidueField
   609	      (p.asIdeal.ResidueField ⊗[P.cover.Carrier] Q) = 1 := by
   610	    rw [← Module.rankAtStalk_eq]
   611	    exact P.h0_rank_one p
   612	  haveI : Nontrivial (p.asIdeal.ResidueField ⊗[P.cover.Carrier] Q) :=
   613	    Module.nontrivial_of_finrank_pos (by rw [hfr]; norm_num)
   614	  haveI : Nontrivial (Q ⊗[P.cover.Carrier] p.asIdeal.ResidueField) :=
   615	    (TensorProduct.comm P.cover.Carrier _ _).toEquiv.symm.nontrivial
   616	  obtain ⟨f, hf, y, hy⟩ :=
   617	    Module.exists_fibrewise_tmul_ne_zero_of_projective p (Q := Q)
   618	      (by infer_instance)
   619	  refine ⟨f, hf, y, ?_, ?_⟩
   620	  · simpa only [Q] using hy
   621	  · exact P.evaluation_evaluationLiftOfH0 y
   622	
   623	/-- The fibrewise-regular local equations cut by a tied local-away datum section.
   624	
   625	The nonvanishing proof is derived by
   626	`sectionsMapTop_datumSectionBaseChange_away_ne_zero`; it is not additional witness data.
   627	Together with `exists_baseOpen_evaluation_generator`, this is the immediate local divisor
   628	consumer on the datum side.  Identifying it with the native evaluation zero locus remains
   629	a separate `O`-module base-change contract. -/
   630	noncomputable def baseOpenDatumSectionLocalEquations
   631	    (P : PicRankOneLocalPresentation pi lam)
   632	    [IsNoetherianRing P.cover.Carrier]
   633	    (f : P.cover.Carrier)
   634	    (y : Sheaf.HModule P.datum.sheaf 0)
   635	    (hy : ∀ p : PrimeSpectrum P.cover.Carrier, f ∉ p.asIdeal →
   636	      (y ⊗ₜ (1 : p.asIdeal.ResidueField) :
   637	        Sheaf.HModule P.datum.sheaf 0 ⊗[P.cover.Carrier]
   638	          p.asIdeal.ResidueField) ≠ 0) :
   639	    (relCurve C (Localization.Away f)).LocalEquations :=
   640	  P.sectionLocalEquationsOfDatumSectionBaseChange
   641	    (Localization.Away f) y
   642	    (fun q => P.sectionsMapTop_datumSectionBaseChange_away_ne_zero f y hy q)
   643	
   644	/-- The local equations cut by the tied datum section represent its base-changed
   645	cocycle datum. -/
   646	theorem baseOpenDatumSectionLocalEquations_picClass
   647	    (P : PicRankOneLocalPresentation pi lam)
   648	    [IsNoetherianRing P.cover.Carrier]
   649	    (f : P.cover.Carrier)
   650	    (y : Sheaf.HModule P.datum.sheaf 0)
   651	    (hy : ∀ p : PrimeSpectrum P.cover.Carrier, f ∉ p.asIdeal →
   652	      (y ⊗ₜ (1 : p.asIdeal.ResidueField) :
   653	        Sheaf.HModule P.datum.sheaf 0 ⊗[P.cover.Carrier]
   654	          p.asIdeal.ResidueField) ≠ 0) :
   655	    (P.baseOpenDatumSectionLocalEquations f y hy).picClass =
   656	      (P.datum.baseChange (Localization.Away f)).cechPicClass := by
   657	  unfold baseOpenDatumSectionLocalEquations
   658	  exact P.sectionLocalEquationsOfDatumSectionBaseChange_picClass
   659	    (Localization.Away f) y
   660	    (fun q => P.sectionsMapTop_datumSectionBaseChange_away_ne_zero f y hy q)
   661	
   662	/-! ## Degree of the tied datum -/
   663	
   664	/- The high-priority `relCurve.instOver` used by the section bridge and the degree stack's
   665	base-change `Over` instance have the same structure morphism but different instance keys.
   666	Re-key the standard base-change bundle locally before stating the degree theorem. -/
   667	noncomputable local instance (priority := 20000) rankOneDegreeOver
   668	    (L : Type u) [Field L] [Algebra k L] :
   669	    (relCurve C L).Over (Spec (.of L)) :=
   670	  instOverBaseChange C L
   671	
   672	noncomputable local instance rankOneDegreeSmooth
   673	    (L : Type u) [Field L] [Algebra k L] :
   674	    SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 (relCurve C L ↘ Spec (.of L)) :=
   675	  instSmoothOfRelativeDimensionBaseChange C L
   676	
   677	noncomputable local instance rankOneDegreeIntegral
   678	    (L : Type u) [Field L] [Algebra k L] :
   679	    IsIntegral (relCurve C L) :=
   680	  instIsIntegralBaseChange C L
   681	
   682	noncomputable local instance rankOneDegreeQuasiCompact
   683	    (L : Type u) [Field L] [Algebra k L] :
   684	    QuasiCompact (relCurve C L ↘ Spec (.of L)) :=
   685	  instQuasiCompactBaseChange C L
   686	
   687	noncomputable local instance rankOneDegreeFiniteH0
   688	    (L : Type u) [Field L] [Algebra k L] :
   689	    Module.Finite L (Sheaf.HModule ((relCurve C L).moduleKSheaf L) 0) :=
   690	  instModuleFiniteHModuleZeroBaseChange C L
   691	
   692	noncomputable local instance rankOneDegreeFiniteH1
   693	    (L : Type u) [Field L] [Algebra k L] :
   694	    Module.Finite L (Sheaf.HModule ((relCurve C L).moduleKSheaf L) 1) :=
   695	  instModuleFiniteHModuleOneBaseChange C L
   696	
   697	/-- The cocycle datum tied to a genus-degree presentation has class degree `genus C`
   698	after every field-valued coefficient extension.
   699	
   700	The proof follows the presentation itself: restrict `lam` to its etale-cover carrier,
   701	identify that class with `representative`, rewrite it as the datum's relative Picard class,
   702	and read the defining degree condition of `lam`. -/
   703	theorem datum_classDeg_baseChange
   704	    (P : PicRankOneLocalPresentation pi lam)
   705	    (L : Type u) [Field L] [Algebra k L] [Algebra P.cover.Carrier L]
   706	    [IsScalarTower k P.cover.Carrier L] :
   707	    classDeg L
   708	      (Scheme.CechPic.map (relCurveMap C P.cover.Carrier L)
   709	        P.datum.cechPicClass) = genus C := by
   710	  let iota : A →ₐ[k] P.cover.Carrier :=
   711	    (Algebra.ofId A P.cover.Carrier).restrictScalars k
   712	  let psi : P.cover.Carrier →ₐ[k] L :=
   713	    (Algebra.ofId P.cover.Carrier L).restrictScalars k
   714	  have hcurve :
   715	      relCurveMap C P.cover.Carrier L =
   716	        (C ◁ Over.overSpecMap psi).left := by
   717	    refine congrArg
   718	      (fun f : overSpec k L ⟶ overSpec k P.cover.Carrier => (C ◁ f).left) ?_
   719	    exact Over.OverMorphism.ext rfl
   720	  have hpresentation :
   721	      picEtMap C (Over.overSpecMap iota) lam.1 =
   722	        relPicToPicEt C (overSpec k P.cover.Carrier)
   723	          (P.representative : relPic C (overSpec k P.cover.Carrier)) := by
   724	    exact picEtMap_eq_relPicToPicEt_of_affineRepresentative
   725	      C lam.1 P.cover P.representative P.represents.symm
   726	  calc
   727	    classDeg L
   728	        (Scheme.CechPic.map (relCurveMap C P.cover.Carrier L)
   729	          P.datum.cechPicClass) =
   730	      relPicDeg L
   731	        (relPicMk C (overSpec k L)
   732	          (Scheme.CechPic.map (relCurveMap C P.cover.Carrier L)
   733	            P.datum.cechPicClass)) :=
   734	      (relPicDeg_relPicMk L _).symm
   735	    _ = relPicDeg L
   736	        (relPicMap C (Over.overSpecMap psi)
   737	          (relPicMk C (overSpec k P.cover.Carrier)
   738	            P.datum.cechPicClass)) := by
   739	      rw [relPicMap_mk, ← hcurve]
   740	      rfl
   741	    _ = relPicDeg L
   742	        (relPicMap C (Over.overSpecMap psi)
   743	          (P.representative : relPic C (overSpec k P.cover.Carrier))) := by
   744	      rw [P.datum_class]
   745	    _ = degAt
   746	        (relPicToPicEt C (overSpec k P.cover.Carrier)
   747	          (P.representative : relPic C (overSpec k P.cover.Carrier)))
   748	        (Over.overSpecMap psi) :=
   749	      (degAt_relPicToPicEt
   750	        (P.representative : relPic C (overSpec k P.cover.Carrier))
   751	        (Over.overSpecMap psi)).symm
   752	    _ = degAt (picEtMap C (Over.overSpecMap iota) lam.1)
   753	        (Over.overSpecMap psi) := by rw [hpresentation]
   754	    _ = degAt lam.1 (Over.overSpecMap psi ≫ Over.overSpecMap iota) :=
   755	      degAt_picEtMap (Over.overSpecMap iota) lam.1 (Over.overSpecMap psi)
   756	    _ = genus C := lam.2 L (Over.overSpecMap psi ≫ Over.overSpecMap iota)
   757	
   758	end PicRankOneLocalPresentation
   759	
   760	end AlgebraicGeometry

    10	
    11	/-!
    12	# Certified divisor families: the DD-1 carrier (`informal/spec-dd-1.md` §1)
    13	
    14	The Wave-4 DAT-D divisor functor's object data over an affine test `R`, the worksheet's
    15	(D1) pin (`informal/dat-d-worksheet.md` §1.1): a `LocalEquations` system `d` on the
    16	relative curve `C_R = relCurve C R`, a **finite chart adaptation** refining it — finitely
    17	many basic opens `D(h_j)` of the two pinned charts with partition witnesses, carrying
    18	regular equations `f_j` that agree with `d`'s equations up to units — and the **colength
    19	certificate**: the chart-local colength modules `Γ(D(h_j))/(f_j)` are finite projective
    20	over `R`, and the glued equalizer module `W(d)` is finite projective of constant fibre
    21	rank `n` (`Module.rankAtStalk`), with the two flat-cokernel clauses (c3)/(c4) that make
    22	certificates base-change (`AlgebraicJacobian.Picard.FlatCokernel`).
    23	
    24	* `AlgebraicGeometry.FinCoverData` — the `Fin`-indexed basic-open cover data (`Type u`;
    25	  DAT-1's `BasicOpenCoverData` shape is `Type (u+1)`, unusable inside a functor value).
    26	* `AlgebraicGeometry.DivisorAdaptation` — the adaptation: equations + the pointwise
    27	  refinement-up-to-units clause `eqn_rel` (point-free, so it pulls back along arbitrary
    28	  morphisms), with the anchored constructor `DivisorAdaptation.ofAnchors`.
    29	* `DivisorAdaptation.gluedSubmodule` — the glued colength module
    30	  `W(d) = ker (δ⁻ − δ⁺) ⊆ Π_j Γ(D(h_j))/(f_j)`, with the equalizer description
    31	  `mem_gluedSubmodule_iff` (the worksheet's `eq(∏_j ⇉ ∏_{j,j'})`).
    32	* `DivisorAdaptation.IsCertified` — the certificate (c1)–(c4).
    33	* `AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.LocalEquations.DivEq` — divisor equality of local-equation
    34	  systems: on a common refinement the equations agree up to units (refinement +
    35	  rescaling in one move), an equivalence relation with
    36	  `picClass_eq_of_divEq` (the class laws `picClass_restrict`/`picClass_rescale`).
    37	* `AlgebraicGeometry.CertifiedDivisorFamily`, `AlgebraicGeometry.DivFam` — the certified
    38	  family and the setoid quotient `DivFam C π n R : Type u`, the divisor functor's value
    39	  on the affine test `R`, with `DivFam.picClass`.
    40	
    41	The `R`-algebra structure on section rings is `Scheme.overSectionsAlgebra` through
    42	`relCurve.instOver` (LOCAL instances, house rule) — consumers must activate the same
    43	instances.
    44	-/
    45	
    46	set_option autoImplicit false
    47	
    48	universe u
    49	
    50	open CategoryTheory TopologicalSpace Opposite
    51	
    52	namespace AlgebraicGeometry
    53	
    54	attribute [local instance] Scheme.overModule Scheme.overSectionsAlgebra
    55	
    56	/-! ## Divisor equality of local-equation systems (the setoid relation)
    57	
    58	Generic in the scheme; this is pure `DivisorClass`-level material. -/
    59	
    60	namespace Scheme.LocalEquations
    61	
    62	variable {X : Scheme.{u}}
    63	
    64	/-- Restriction of a section along `W ≤ V ≤ U` composes to restriction along `W ≤ U`. -/
    65	private lemma res_res {W V U : X.Opens} (h₁ : W ≤ V) (h₂ : V ≤ U) (s : Γ(X, U)) :
    66	    (X.presheaf.map (homOfLE h₁).op).hom ((X.presheaf.map (homOfLE h₂).op).hom s)
    67	      = (X.presheaf.map (homOfLE (h₁.trans h₂)).op).hom s := by
    68	  rw [← CommRingCat.comp_apply, ← Functor.map_comp, ← op_comp, homOfLE_comp]
    69	
    70	/-- **Divisor equality** of two local-equation systems: on a common refinement of the
    71	two covers, the equations agree up to a unit at every point — common refinement plus
    72	unit rescaling in a single move (the `CechPic`-pattern setoid of the DD-1 spec). -/
    73	def DivEq (d₁ d₂ : X.LocalEquations) : Prop :=
    74	  ∃ (𝒲 : X.PointedCover) (h₁ : 𝒲 ≤ d₁.cover) (h₂ : 𝒲 ≤ d₂.cover),
    75	    ∀ x : X, ∃ u : Γ(X, 𝒲.opens x)ˣ,
    76	      (X.presheaf.map (homOfLE (h₁ x)).op).hom (d₁.eqn x)
    77	        = (u : Γ(X, 𝒲.opens x))
    78	          * (X.presheaf.map (homOfLE (h₂ x)).op).hom (d₂.eqn x)
    79	
    80	lemma divEq_refl (d : X.LocalEquations) : DivEq d d :=
    81	  ⟨d.cover, le_rfl, le_rfl, fun _ => ⟨1, by rw [Units.val_one, one_mul]⟩⟩
    82	
    83	lemma DivEq.symm {d₁ d₂ : X.LocalEquations} (h : DivEq d₁ d₂) : DivEq d₂ d₁ := by
    84	  obtain ⟨𝒲, h₁, h₂, H⟩ := h
    85	  refine ⟨𝒲, h₂, h₁, fun x => ?_⟩
    86	  obtain ⟨u, hu⟩ := H x
    87	  exact ⟨u⁻¹, by
    88	    rw [hu, ← mul_assoc, ← Units.val_mul, inv_mul_cancel, Units.val_one, one_mul]⟩
    89	
    90	lemma DivEq.trans {d₁ d₂ d₃ : X.LocalEquations} (h : DivEq d₁ d₂) (h' : DivEq d₂ d₃) :
    91	    DivEq d₁ d₃ := by
    92	  obtain ⟨𝒲, h₁, h₂, H⟩ := h
    93	  obtain ⟨𝒱, k₂, k₃, K⟩ := h'
    94	  refine ⟨𝒲 ⊓ 𝒱, fun x => (inf_le_left (b := 𝒱.opens x)).trans (h₁ x),
    95	    fun x => (inf_le_right (a := 𝒲.opens x)).trans (k₃ x), fun x => ?_⟩
    96	  obtain ⟨u, hu⟩ := H x
    97	  obtain ⟨v, hv⟩ := K x
    98	  have E1 := congrArg (X.presheaf.map (homOfLE
    99	    (inf_le_left : 𝒲.opens x ⊓ 𝒱.opens x ≤ 𝒲.opens x)).op).hom hu
   100	  rw [map_mul, res_res, res_res] at E1
   101	  have E2 := congrArg (X.presheaf.map (homOfLE
   102	    (inf_le_right : 𝒲.opens x ⊓ 𝒱.opens x ≤ 𝒱.opens x)).op).hom hv
   103	  rw [map_mul, res_res, res_res] at E2
   104	  refine ⟨X.unitsRestrict inf_le_left u * X.unitsRestrict inf_le_right v, ?_⟩
   105	  have hcast : ∀ (w : Γ(X, 𝒲.opens x ⊓ 𝒱.opens x)ˣ), (w : Γ(X, 𝒲.opens x ⊓ 𝒱.opens x))
   106	      = w.val := fun _ => rfl
   107	  rw [Units.val_mul]
   108	  calc (X.presheaf.map (homOfLE _).op).hom (d₁.eqn x)
   109	      = (X.unitsRestrict inf_le_left u).val
   110	        * (X.presheaf.map (homOfLE ((inf_le_right).trans (k₂ x))).op).hom (d₂.eqn x) := by
   111	        rw [show (X.unitsRestrict (inf_le_left :
   112	            𝒲.opens x ⊓ 𝒱.opens x ≤ 𝒲.opens x) u).val
   113	            = (X.presheaf.map (homOfLE (inf_le_left :
   114	                𝒲.opens x ⊓ 𝒱.opens x ≤ 𝒲.opens x)).op).hom u.val from rfl]
   115	        exact E1
   116	    _ = (X.unitsRestrict inf_le_left u).val * ((X.unitsRestrict inf_le_right v).val
   117	        * (X.presheaf.map (homOfLE ((inf_le_right).trans (k₃ x))).op).hom (d₃.eqn x)) := by
   118	        rw [show (X.unitsRestrict (inf_le_right :
   119	            𝒲.opens x ⊓ 𝒱.opens x ≤ 𝒱.opens x) v).val
   120	            = (X.presheaf.map (homOfLE (inf_le_right :
   121	                𝒲.opens x ⊓ 𝒱.opens x ≤ 𝒱.opens x)).op).hom v.val from rfl]
   122	        rw [E2]
   123	    _ = (X.unitsRestrict inf_le_left u).val * (X.unitsRestrict inf_le_right v).val
   124	        * (X.presheaf.map (homOfLE _).op).hom (d₃.eqn x) := by
   125	        rw [mul_assoc]
   126	
   127	/-- Structure extensionality for local-equation systems: the two `Prop` fields are
   128	proof-irrelevant, so a system is determined by its cover and equations. -/
   129	private lemma ext_eqn {d e : X.LocalEquations} (hcov : d.cover = e.cover)
   130	    (heqn : d.eqn ≍ e.eqn) : d = e := by
   131	  cases d; cases e
   132	  cases hcov; cases heqn
   133	  rfl

   135	/-- **Divisor equality preserves the Picard class** (`𝒪(D)` depends only on the divisor):
   136	restrict both systems to the common refinement (`picClass_restrict`), where they differ
   137	by a unit rescaling (`picClass_rescale`). -/
   138	theorem picClass_eq_of_divEq {d₁ d₂ : X.LocalEquations} (h : DivEq d₁ d₂) :
   139	    d₁.picClass = d₂.picClass := by
   140	  obtain ⟨𝒲, h₁, h₂, H⟩ := h
   141	  rw [← d₁.picClass_restrict 𝒲 h₁, ← d₂.picClass_restrict 𝒲 h₂]
   142	  have hres : d₁.restrict 𝒲 h₁ = (d₂.restrict 𝒲 h₂).rescale (fun x => (H x).choose) := by
   143	    refine ext_eqn rfl (heq_of_eq (funext fun x => ?_))
   144	    exact (H x).choose_spec
   145	  rw [hres, picClass_rescale]
   146

   149	/-! ## The finite chart adaptation -/
   150	
   151	variable {k : Type u} [Field k] (C : Over (Spec (.of k)))
   152	variable (R : Type u) [CommRing R] [Algebra k R]
   153	variable (π : C.left ⟶ P1 k)
   154	
   155	/-- **The `Fin`-indexed basic-open cover data** of the two pinned charts of the relative
   156	curve (`informal/spec-dd-1.md` §1a): `m₀ + m₁` basic-open generators with partition
   157	witnesses. The DAT-1 datum `BasicOpenCoverData` carries `Type u` index fields and hence
   158	lives in `Type (u+1)`; this `Fin`-indexed form is the `Type u` carrier a functor value
   159	can quotient. -/
   160	structure FinCoverData [IsAffineHom π] : Type u where
   161	  /-- The number of chart-0 pieces. -/
   162	  m₀ : ℕ
   163	  /-- The number of chart-1 pieces. -/
   164	  m₁ : ℕ
   165	  /-- The chart-0 basic-open generators. -/
   166	  h₀ : Fin m₀ → Γ(relCurve C R, (relCover C R (fiberTwoCover π)).V₀)
   167	  /-- The chart-1 basic-open generators. -/
   168	  h₁ : Fin m₁ → Γ(relCurve C R, (relCover C R (fiberTwoCover π)).V₁)
   169	  /-- The chart-0 partition coefficients. -/
   170	  a₀ : Fin m₀ → Γ(relCurve C R, (relCover C R (fiberTwoCover π)).V₀)
   171	  /-- The chart-1 partition coefficients. -/
   172	  a₁ : Fin m₁ → Γ(relCurve C R, (relCover C R (fiberTwoCover π)).V₁)
   173	  /-- The chart-0 partition witness. -/
   174	  partition₀ : ∑ j : Fin m₀, a₀ j * h₀ j = 1
   175	  /-- The chart-1 partition witness. -/
   176	  partition₁ : ∑ j : Fin m₁, a₁ j * h₁ j = 1
   177	
   178	namespace FinCoverData
   179	
   180	variable {C R π} [IsAffineHom π] (D : FinCoverData C R π)
   181	
   182	/-- The gluing index of the adaptation, `Fin m₀ ⊕ Fin m₁`. -/
   183	abbrev index : Type := Fin D.m₀ ⊕ Fin D.m₁
   184	
   185	/-- The pieces: the basic opens `D(h_j)` of the two pinned charts. -/
   186	noncomputable def pieces : D.index → (relCurve C R).Opens :=
   187	  Sum.elim (fun j => (relCurve C R).basicOpen (D.h₀ j))
   188	    (fun j => (relCurve C R).basicOpen (D.h₁ j))
   189	
   190	@[simp]
   191	lemma pieces_inl (j : Fin D.m₀) :
   192	    D.pieces (Sum.inl j) = (relCurve C R).basicOpen (D.h₀ j) := rfl
   193	
   194	@[simp]
   195	lemma pieces_inr (j : Fin D.m₁) :
   196	    D.pieces (Sum.inr j) = (relCurve C R).basicOpen (D.h₁ j) := rfl
   197	
   198	/-- The chart-0 pieces cover the pinned chart `V₀ᴿ`. -/
   199	lemma cover₀ : (relCover C R (fiberTwoCover π)).V₀ ≤
   200	    ⨆ j : Fin D.m₀, (relCurve C R).basicOpen (D.h₀ j) :=
   201	  le_iSup_basicOpen_of_sum_eq_one D.a₀ D.h₀ D.partition₀
   202	
   203	/-- The chart-1 pieces cover the pinned chart `V₁ᴿ`. -/
   204	lemma cover₁ : (relCover C R (fiberTwoCover π)).V₁ ≤
   205	    ⨆ j : Fin D.m₁, (relCurve C R).basicOpen (D.h₁ j) :=
   206	  le_iSup_basicOpen_of_sum_eq_one D.a₁ D.h₁ D.partition₁
   207	
   208	end FinCoverData
   209	
   210	/-- Restriction of sections of the relative curve as an `R`-algebra homomorphism
   211	(`Scheme.overSectionsAlgebra` structures on both sides). -/
   212	noncomputable def relResAlgHom {W V : (relCurve C R).Opens} (h : W ≤ V) :
   213	    Γ(relCurve C R, V) →ₐ[R] Γ(relCurve C R, W) :=
   214	  AlgHom.mk' (CommRingCat.Hom.hom ((relCurve C R).presheaf.map (homOfLE h).op))
   215	    (fun c x => by
   216	      simp only [Algebra.smul_def]
   217	      rw [map_mul]
   218	      congr 1
   219	      rw [Scheme.algebraMap_overSectionsAlgebra, Scheme.algebraMap_overSectionsAlgebra]
   220	      exact (relCurve C R).overAlgebraMap_apply_res R (homOfLE h).op c)
   221	
   222	@[simp]
   223	lemma relResAlgHom_apply {W V : (relCurve C R).Opens} (h : W ≤ V) (s : Γ(relCurve C R, V)) :
   224	    relResAlgHom C R h s = ((relCurve C R).presheaf.map (homOfLE h).op).hom s :=
   225	  rfl
   226	
   227	/-- **The finite chart adaptation of a local-equation system** (worksheet §1.1 (D1)):
   228	basic-open cover data of the two pinned charts, equations `f_j` on the pieces, and the
   229	pointwise refinement clause `eqn_rel` — on the overlap of each piece with any member of
   230	`d.cover`, `f_j` agrees with `d`'s equation up to a unit. Regularity of the `f_j` is
   231	DERIVED (`DivisorAdaptation.eqn_regular`), not stored. -/
   232	structure DivisorAdaptation [IsAffineHom π] (d : (relCurve C R).LocalEquations) :
   233	    Type u extends FinCoverData C R π where
   234	  /-- The equation on the piece `D(h_j)`. -/
   235	  eqn : ∀ j : toFinCoverData.index, Γ(relCurve C R, toFinCoverData.pieces j)
   236	  /-- The equations refine `d` pointwise up to units: on the overlap of each piece with
   237	  any member of `d`'s cover, `f_j` and `d`'s equation differ by a unit. Point-free (the
   238	  `DivEq` spelling), so it pulls back along arbitrary morphisms — the resolution of the
   239	  DD-1 pt-transport seam (`informal/spec-dd-2.md` §1a). The quantifier ranges over ALL
   240	  `y`: the empty overlap carries the zero ring, where the clause is trivial. -/
   241	  eqn_rel : ∀ (j : toFinCoverData.index) (y : relCurve C R),
   242	    ∃ u : Γ(relCurve C R, toFinCoverData.pieces j ⊓ d.cover.opens y)ˣ,
   243	      ((relCurve C R).presheaf.map (homOfLE inf_le_left).op).hom (eqn j)
   244	        = (u : Γ(relCurve C R, toFinCoverData.pieces j ⊓ d.cover.opens y))
   245	          * ((relCurve C R).presheaf.map (homOfLE inf_le_right).op).hom (d.eqn y)
   246	
   247	namespace DivisorAdaptation
   248	
   249	variable {C R π} [IsAffineHom π] {d : (relCurve C R).LocalEquations}
   250	variable (A : DivisorAdaptation C R π d)
   251	
   252	/-- **The compatibility constructor from anchored refinement data** (the pre-DD-2 field
   253	layout): a base point `pt j` of `d.cover` per piece with `pieces j ≤ d.cover.opens (pt j)`
   254	and a comparison unit `eqn j = unit j · res (d.eqn (pt j))`. The pointwise clause
   255	`eqn_rel` is derived by rewriting `d.eqn (pt j)` into `d.eqn y` through the transition
   256	unit `d.ratioUnit (pt j) y` on the overlap (the `DivEq.trans` calc pattern). -/
   257	def ofAnchors (D : FinCoverData C R π)
   258	    (eqn : ∀ j : D.index, Γ(relCurve C R, D.pieces j))
   259	    (pt : D.index → relCurve C R)
   260	    (piece_le : ∀ j, D.pieces j ≤ d.cover.opens (pt j))
   261	    (unit : ∀ j, Γ(relCurve C R, D.pieces j)ˣ)
   262	    (eqn_eq : ∀ j, eqn j = (unit j : Γ(relCurve C R, D.pieces j))
   263	      * ((relCurve C R).presheaf.map (homOfLE (piece_le j)).op).hom (d.eqn (pt j))) :
   264	    DivisorAdaptation C R π d where
   265	  toFinCoverData := D
   266	  eqn := eqn
   267	  eqn_rel := fun j y => by
   268	    have hWle : D.pieces j ⊓ d.cover.opens y
   269	        ≤ d.cover.opens (pt j) ⊓ d.cover.opens y :=
   270	      inf_le_inf (piece_le j) le_rfl
   271	    have E1 := congrArg ((relCurve C R).presheaf.map (homOfLE
   272	      (inf_le_left : D.pieces j ⊓ d.cover.opens y ≤ D.pieces j)).op).hom (eqn_eq j)
   273	    rw [map_mul, Scheme.LocalEquations.res_res] at E1
   274	    have E2 := congrArg ((relCurve C R).presheaf.map (homOfLE hWle).op).hom
   275	      (d.eqn_restrict_eq (pt j) y)
   276	    rw [map_mul, Scheme.LocalEquations.res_res, Scheme.LocalEquations.res_res] at E2
   277	    refine ⟨(relCurve C R).unitsRestrict inf_le_left (unit j)
   278	      * (relCurve C R).unitsRestrict hWle (d.ratioUnit (pt j) y), ?_⟩
   279	    rw [Units.val_mul]
   280	    calc ((relCurve C R).presheaf.map (homOfLE inf_le_left).op).hom (eqn j)
   281	        = ((relCurve C R).unitsRestrict inf_le_left (unit j)).val
   282	          * ((relCurve C R).presheaf.map (homOfLE
   283	              ((inf_le_left : D.pieces j ⊓ d.cover.opens y ≤ D.pieces j).trans
   284	                (piece_le j))).op).hom (d.eqn (pt j)) := by
   285	          rw [show ((relCurve C R).unitsRestrict (inf_le_left :
   286	              D.pieces j ⊓ d.cover.opens y ≤ D.pieces j) (unit j)).val
   287	              = ((relCurve C R).presheaf.map (homOfLE (inf_le_left :
   288	                  D.pieces j ⊓ d.cover.opens y ≤ D.pieces j)).op).hom (unit j).val
   289	            from rfl]
   290	          exact E1
   291	      _ = ((relCurve C R).unitsRestrict inf_le_left (unit j)).val
   292	          * (((relCurve C R).unitsRestrict hWle (d.ratioUnit (pt j) y)).val
   293	            * ((relCurve C R).presheaf.map (homOfLE (hWle.trans
   294	                (inf_le_right : d.cover.opens (pt j) ⊓ d.cover.opens y
   295	                  ≤ d.cover.opens y))).op).hom (d.eqn y)) := by
   296	          rw [show ((relCurve C R).unitsRestrict hWle (d.ratioUnit (pt j) y)).val
   297	              = ((relCurve C R).presheaf.map
   298	                  (homOfLE hWle).op).hom (d.ratioUnit (pt j) y).val from rfl]
   299	          rw [E2]
   300	      _ = ((relCurve C R).unitsRestrict inf_le_left (unit j)).val
   301	          * ((relCurve C R).unitsRestrict hWle (d.ratioUnit (pt j) y)).val
   302	          * ((relCurve C R).presheaf.map (homOfLE
   303	              (inf_le_right : D.pieces j ⊓ d.cover.opens y
   304	                ≤ d.cover.opens y)).op).hom (d.eqn y) := by
   305	          rw [mul_assoc]
   306	
   307	/-- The adaptation's equations are regular: at `z ∈ D(h_j)` the pointwise clause
   308	`eqn_rel j z` presents the germ of `f_j` as a unit germ times the germ of `d`'s regular
   309	equation at the member of `z` itself. -/
   310	theorem eqn_regular (j : A.index) (z : relCurve C R) (hz : z ∈ A.pieces j) :
   311	    ((relCurve C R).presheaf.germ (A.pieces j) z hz).hom (A.eqn j)
   312	      ∈ nonZeroDivisors ((relCurve C R).presheaf.stalk z) := by
   313	  obtain ⟨u, hu⟩ := A.eqn_rel j z
   314	  have hzW : z ∈ A.pieces j ⊓ d.cover.opens z := ⟨hz, d.cover.mem_opens z⟩
   315	  have hgerm : ((relCurve C R).presheaf.germ (A.pieces j) z hz).hom (A.eqn j)
   316	      = ((relCurve C R).presheaf.germ (A.pieces j ⊓ d.cover.opens z) z hzW).hom
   317	          (u : Γ(relCurve C R, A.pieces j ⊓ d.cover.opens z))
   318	        * ((relCurve C R).presheaf.germ (d.cover.opens z) z
   319	            (d.cover.mem_opens z)).hom (d.eqn z) := by
   320	    have h := congrArg ((relCurve C R).presheaf.germ
   321	      (A.pieces j ⊓ d.cover.opens z) z hzW).hom hu
   322	    rw [map_mul, TopCat.Presheaf.germ_res_apply, TopCat.Presheaf.germ_res_apply] at h
   323	    exact h
   324	  rw [hgerm]
   325	  exact mul_mem
   326	    ((u.isUnit.map ((relCurve C R).presheaf.germ
   327	      (A.pieces j ⊓ d.cover.opens z) z hzW).hom).mem_nonZeroDivisors)
   328	    (d.regular z z (d.cover.mem_opens z))
   329	
   330	/-! ### The colength modules and the glued equalizer -/
   331	
   332	/-- The chart-local colength module `Γ(D(h_j)) ⧸ (f_j)`, an `R`-algebra through
   333	`Scheme.overSectionsAlgebra`. -/
   334	noncomputable abbrev colength (j : A.index) : Type u :=
   335	  Γ(relCurve C R, A.pieces j) ⧸ Ideal.span {A.eqn j}
   336	
   337	/-- The symmetric overlap ideal: both equations restricted to the piece overlap. The
   338	two restrictions generate the same ideal (the equations differ by units on overlaps
   339	through the refinement witness), but the symmetric span needs no transport in the
   340	DEFINITION. -/
   341	noncomputable abbrev ovlIdeal (i j : A.index) :
   342	    Ideal Γ(relCurve C R, A.pieces i ⊓ A.pieces j) :=
   343	  Ideal.span
   344	    {relResAlgHom C R (inf_le_left : A.pieces i ⊓ A.pieces j ≤ A.pieces i) (A.eqn i),
   345	     relResAlgHom C R (inf_le_right : A.pieces i ⊓ A.pieces j ≤ A.pieces j) (A.eqn j)}
   346	
   347	/-- The overlap colength module `Γ(D(h_i) ⊓ D(h_j)) ⧸ (f_i, f_j)`. -/
   348	noncomputable abbrev ovlColength (i j : A.index) : Type u :=
   349	  Γ(relCurve C R, A.pieces i ⊓ A.pieces j) ⧸ A.ovlIdeal i j
   350	
   351	/-- The induced `R`-algebra map `colength i → ovlColength i j` (restrict, then quotient;
   352	the ideal of `f_i` lands in the symmetric span). -/
   353	noncomputable def toOvlLeft (i j : A.index) : A.colength i →ₐ[R] A.ovlColength i j :=
   354	  Ideal.Quotient.liftₐ (Ideal.span {A.eqn i})
   355	    ((Ideal.Quotient.mkₐ R (A.ovlIdeal i j)).comp (relResAlgHom C R inf_le_left))
   356	    (by
   357	      intro a ha
   358	      rw [Ideal.mem_span_singleton] at ha
   359	      obtain ⟨c, rfl⟩ := ha
   360	      simp only [AlgHom.comp_apply, map_mul]
   361	      have hmem : relResAlgHom C R
   362	          (inf_le_left : A.pieces i ⊓ A.pieces j ≤ A.pieces i) (A.eqn i)
   363	          ∈ A.ovlIdeal i j :=
   364	        Ideal.subset_span (Set.mem_insert _ _)
   365	      rw [Ideal.Quotient.mkₐ_eq_mk, Ideal.Quotient.eq_zero_iff_mem.mpr hmem, zero_mul])
   366	
   367	/-- The induced `R`-algebra map `colength j → ovlColength i j`. -/
   368	noncomputable def toOvlRight (i j : A.index) : A.colength j →ₐ[R] A.ovlColength i j :=
   369	  Ideal.Quotient.liftₐ (Ideal.span {A.eqn j})
   370	    ((Ideal.Quotient.mkₐ R (A.ovlIdeal i j)).comp (relResAlgHom C R inf_le_right))
   371	    (by
   372	      intro a ha
   373	      rw [Ideal.mem_span_singleton] at ha
   374	      obtain ⟨c, rfl⟩ := ha
   375	      simp only [AlgHom.comp_apply, map_mul]
   376	      have hmem : relResAlgHom C R
   377	          (inf_le_right : A.pieces i ⊓ A.pieces j ≤ A.pieces j) (A.eqn j)
   378	          ∈ A.ovlIdeal i j :=
   379	        Ideal.subset_span (Set.mem_insert_of_mem _ rfl)
   380	      rw [Ideal.Quotient.mkₐ_eq_mk, Ideal.Quotient.eq_zero_iff_mem.mpr hmem, zero_mul])
   381	
   382	/-- The product of the chart-local colength modules (an `abbrev`, so the `Pi.module`
   383	instances apply directly — probe finding, spec §1b(iii)). -/
   384	noncomputable abbrev chartProd : Type u := ∀ j : A.index, A.colength j
   385	
   386	/-- The product of the overlap colength modules over ordered index pairs. -/
   387	noncomputable abbrev ovlProd : Type u := ∀ p : A.index × A.index, A.ovlColength p.1 p.2
   388	
   389	/-- The left arrow of the equalizer: restrict the `p.1` component to each overlap. -/
   390	noncomputable def deltaLeft : A.chartProd →ₗ[R] A.ovlProd :=
   391	  LinearMap.pi
   392	    (fun p : A.index × A.index => (A.toOvlLeft p.1 p.2).toLinearMap ∘ₗ LinearMap.proj p.1)
   393	
   394	/-- The right arrow of the equalizer: restrict the `p.2` component to each overlap. -/
   395	noncomputable def deltaRight : A.chartProd →ₗ[R] A.ovlProd :=
   396	  LinearMap.pi
   397	    (fun p : A.index × A.index => (A.toOvlRight p.1 p.2).toLinearMap ∘ₗ LinearMap.proj p.2)
   398	
   399	/-- **The glued colength module `W(d)`** (worksheet §1.1 (c2)): the equalizer of the two
   400	overlap-restriction arrows on the product of chart-local colengths, spelled as the
   401	kernel of their difference (so the `FlatCokernel` base-change keystone applies
   402	verbatim); the equalizer description is `mem_gluedSubmodule_iff`. -/
   403	noncomputable def gluedSubmodule : Submodule R A.chartProd :=
   404	  LinearMap.ker (A.deltaLeft - A.deltaRight)
   405	
   406	/-- The equalizer description of the glued colength module: componentwise agreement of
   407	the two overlap restrictions. -/
   408	lemma mem_gluedSubmodule_iff (s : A.chartProd) :
   409	    s ∈ A.gluedSubmodule ↔ ∀ p : A.index × A.index,
   410	      A.toOvlLeft p.1 p.2 (s p.1) = A.toOvlRight p.1 p.2 (s p.2) := by
   411	  simp only [gluedSubmodule, LinearMap.mem_ker, LinearMap.sub_apply, sub_eq_zero,
   412	    funext_iff, deltaLeft, deltaRight, LinearMap.pi_apply, LinearMap.coe_comp,
   413	    Function.comp_apply, LinearMap.proj_apply, AlgHom.toLinearMap_apply]
   414	
   415	/-- The glued colength module, as a type. -/
   416	noncomputable abbrev Glued : Type u := ↥A.gluedSubmodule
   417	
   418	/-! ### The certificate -/
   419	
   420	/-- **The colength certificate** (worksheet §1.1 (c1)/(c2) in the spec-dd-1 §1c frozen
   421	spelling): chart-local colengths finite projective over `R` (c1); the glued module
   422	finite projective of constant fibre rank `n` — honest finrank at every prime through
   423	`Module.rankAtStalk` (c2); and the two flat-cokernel clauses (c3)/(c4) that make
   424	certificates base-change along ARBITRARY test maps (trivial over a field; transported
   425	by right-exactness; consumed by `FlatCokernel.tensorKer_bijective_of_flat_coker`). -/
   426	structure IsCertified (n : ℕ) : Prop where
   427	  /-- (c1) Each chart-local colength module is a finite `R`-module. -/
   428	  finite_colength : ∀ j, Module.Finite R (A.colength j)
   429	  /-- (c1) Each chart-local colength module is projective over `R`. -/
   430	  projective_colength : ∀ j, Module.Projective R (A.colength j)
   431	  /-- (c2) The glued colength module is a finite `R`-module. -/
   432	  finite_glued : Module.Finite R A.Glued
   433	  /-- (c2) The glued colength module is projective over `R`. -/
   434	  projective_glued : Module.Projective R A.Glued
   435	  /-- (c2) The glued colength module has constant fibre rank `n`. -/
   436	  rankAtStalk_glued : ∀ p : PrimeSpectrum R, Module.rankAtStalk A.Glued p = n
   437	  /-- (c3) The cokernel of `W(d) ↪ Π_j colength j` is flat. -/
   438	  flat_coker_incl : Module.Flat R (A.chartProd ⧸ A.gluedSubmodule)
   439	  /-- (c4) The cokernel of the difference arrow is flat. -/
   440	  flat_coker_diff :
   441	    Module.Flat R (A.ovlProd ⧸ LinearMap.range (A.deltaLeft - A.deltaRight))
   442	
   443	end DivisorAdaptation
   444	
   445	/-! ## The certified family and the divisor-functor value -/
   446	
   447	variable (n : ℕ)
   448	
   449	/-- **A certified divisor family of degree `n` over the test ring `R`** (the worksheet's
   450	(D1) pair `(d, c)`): a local-equation system with a certified finite chart
   451	adaptation. -/
   452	structure CertifiedDivisorFamily [IsAffineHom π] : Type u where
   453	  /-- The local-equation system on the relative curve. -/
   454	  eqns : (relCurve C R).LocalEquations
   455	  /-- The finite chart adaptation refining it. -/
   456	  adaptation : DivisorAdaptation C R π eqns
   457	  /-- The colength certificate of degree `n`. -/
   458	  certified : adaptation.IsCertified n
   459	
   460	/-- The divisor-equality setoid on certified families: the underlying local-equation
   461	systems cut the same divisor (`Scheme.LocalEquations.DivEq`); the adaptation and
   462	certificate are per-representative data and do not enter the relation. -/
   463	def divFamSetoid [IsAffineHom π] : Setoid (CertifiedDivisorFamily C R π n) where
   464	  r F G := Scheme.LocalEquations.DivEq F.eqns G.eqns
   465	  iseqv :=
   466	    ⟨fun F => Scheme.LocalEquations.divEq_refl F.eqns,
   467	     fun h => h.symm, fun h h' => h.trans h'⟩
   468	
   469	/-- **The divisor-functor value on the affine test `R`** (worksheet §1.1): certified
   470	divisor families of degree `n` up to divisor equality. A `Type u` quotient — the
   471	carrier the affine-opens-limit vehicle ranges over. -/
   472	def DivFam [IsAffineHom π] : Type u := Quotient (divFamSetoid C R π n)
   473	
   474	namespace DivFam
   475	
   476	variable {C R π n} [IsAffineHom π]
   477	
   478	/-- The class of a certified family. -/
   479	def mk (F : CertifiedDivisorFamily C R π n) : DivFam C R π n :=
   480	  Quotient.mk (divFamSetoid C R π n) F
   481	
   482	lemma mk_eq_mk_iff {F G : CertifiedDivisorFamily C R π n} :
   483	    mk F = mk G ↔ Scheme.LocalEquations.DivEq F.eqns G.eqns :=
   484	  Quotient.eq (r := divFamSetoid C R π n)
   485	
   486	/-- **The Picard class of a divisor family** `𝒪(D)`: well defined on the quotient by
   487	the class laws (`picClass_eq_of_divEq`). This is the Abel hook DAT-C consumes. -/
   488	noncomputable def picClass (F : DivFam C R π n) : (relCurve C R).CechPic :=
   489	  Quotient.lift (fun F : CertifiedDivisorFamily C R π n => F.eqns.picClass)
   490	    (fun _ _ h => Scheme.LocalEquations.picClass_eq_of_divEq h) F
   491	
   492	@[simp]
   493	lemma picClass_mk (F : CertifiedDivisorFamily C R π n) :
   494	    picClass (mk F) = F.eqns.picClass :=
   495	  rfl
   496	
   497	end DivFam
   498	
   499	end AlgebraicGeometry

161 AlgebraicJacobian/Picard/DivSchemeRedesignChartReadIdeal.lean
     1	/-

     3	Released under Apache 2.0 license as described in the file LICENSE.
     4	Authors: The AlgebraicJacobian Contributors
     5	-/
     6	import AlgebraicJacobian.Picard.DivSchemeRedesignRDNChart
     7	
     8	/-!
     9	# DD-4 redesign: the chart-reading ideal and its colength image
    10	
    11	The chart reading map is only `R`-linear.  Its `R`-linear range is therefore not the ideal
    12	generated by its readings in the chart ring `B = Γ(V)`.  This file records the actual
    13	`B`-ideal and the scalar-extension maps that present its underlying `B`-modules:
    14	
    15	* `chartReadIdeal K b = Ideal.span (range (chartReadMap K b))`;
    16	* `chartReadIdealMap K b : B ⊗[R] K →ₗ[B] B`, whose range is `chartReadIdeal K b`;
    17	* `chartIdealColengthModule K b s`, the image of `chartReadIdeal K b` in
    18	  `B ⧸ Ideal.span {read s}`;
    19	* `chartIdealColengthMap K b s`, whose range is that image.
    20	
    21	The last module agrees with the previously landed `chartColengthModule`.  No flatness or
    22	fibre-injectivity statement is made here: those properties for the `R`-linear range do not
    23	automatically pass to this `B`-ideal.
    24	-/
    25	
    26	set_option autoImplicit false
    27	set_option backward.isDefEq.respectTransparency false
    28	
    29	universe uR uB uM uN u
    30	
    31	open CategoryTheory TopologicalSpace Opposite
    32	open scoped TensorProduct
    33	
    34	namespace LinearMap
    35	
    36	/-- The range of scalar extension is the span, over the new scalar ring, of the original
    37	range.  In particular, this is the precise map presenting the ideal generated by an
    38	`R`-linear family of elements of an `R`-algebra. -/
    39	theorem range_liftBaseChange_eq_span
    40	    {R : Type uR} {B : Type uB} {M : Type uM} {N : Type uN}
    41	    [CommRing R] [CommRing B] [Algebra R B]
    42	    [AddCommGroup M] [Module R M]
    43	    [AddCommGroup N] [Module R N] [Module B N] [IsScalarTower R B N]
    44	    (f : M →ₗ[R] N) :
    45	    LinearMap.range (LinearMap.liftBaseChange B f) =
    46	      Submodule.span B (Set.range f) := by
    47	  apply le_antisymm
    48	  · rintro y ⟨x, rfl⟩
    49	    induction x using TensorProduct.induction_on with
    50	    | zero => exact Submodule.zero_mem _
    51	    | add x y hx hy =>
    52	        simpa only [map_add] using Submodule.add_mem _ hx hy
    53	    | tmul b m =>
    54	        rw [LinearMap.liftBaseChange_tmul]
    55	        exact Submodule.smul_mem _ b (Submodule.subset_span ⟨m, rfl⟩)
    56	  · rw [Submodule.span_le]
    57	    rintro _ ⟨m, rfl⟩
    58	    exact ⟨(1 : B) ⊗ₜ[R] m, by
    59	      rw [LinearMap.liftBaseChange_tmul, one_smul]⟩
    60	
    61	end LinearMap
    62	
    63	namespace AlgebraicGeometry
    64	
    65	attribute [local instance] Scheme.overModule Scheme.overSectionsAlgebra
    66	
    67	variable {k : Type u} [Field k] {C : Over (Spec (.of k))}
    68	variable {R : Type u} [CommRing R] [Algebra k R]
    69	variable {π : C.left ⟶ P1 k} [IsFinite π] {a : ℕ}
    70	
    71	namespace ThetaGeneratorSeed
    72	
    73	/-- The genuine chart-ring ideal generated by the readings of `K`.  This is generally larger
    74	than the `R`-linear range of `chartReadMap K b`. -/
    75	noncomputable def chartReadIdeal
    76	    (K : Submodule R (relThetaSections C R π a)) (b : Bool) :
    77	    Ideal Γ(relCurve C R, relPinnedChart C R π b) :=
    78	  Ideal.span (Set.range (chartReadMap K b))
    79	
    80	/-- The minimal scalar-extension map presenting the ideal generated by the chart readings:
    81	`c ⊗ ψ ↦ c · read(ψ)`. -/
    82	noncomputable def chartReadIdealMap
    83	    (K : Submodule R (relThetaSections C R π a)) (b : Bool) :
    84	    Γ(relCurve C R, relPinnedChart C R π b) ⊗[R] ↥K →ₗ[Γ(relCurve C R,
    85	      relPinnedChart C R π b)] Γ(relCurve C R, relPinnedChart C R π b) :=
    86	  LinearMap.liftBaseChange Γ(relCurve C R, relPinnedChart C R π b) (chartReadMap K b)
    87	
    88	set_option maxHeartbeats 800000 in
    89	/-- The range of `chartReadIdealMap` is exactly the genuine chart-reading ideal. -/
    90	theorem range_chartReadIdealMap
    91	    (K : Submodule R (relThetaSections C R π a)) (b : Bool) :
    92	    LinearMap.range (chartReadIdealMap K b) = chartReadIdeal K b := by
    93	  simpa only [chartReadIdealMap, chartReadIdeal] using
    94	    (LinearMap.range_liftBaseChange_eq_span
    95	      (R := R) (B := Γ(relCurve C R, relPinnedChart C R π b))
    96	      (M := ↥K) (N := Γ(relCurve C R, relPinnedChart C R π b))
    97	      (chartReadMap K b))
    98	
    99	/-- The image of the genuine chart-reading ideal in the colength ring
   100	`B ⧸ Ideal.span {read s}`.  Equivalently, this is `(chartReadIdeal K b + (read s)) / (read s)`,
   101	viewed as a `B`-submodule of the quotient. -/
   102	noncomputable def chartIdealColengthModule
   103	    (K : Submodule R (relThetaSections C R π a)) (b : Bool)
   104	    (s : relThetaSections C R π a) :
   105	    Submodule Γ(relCurve C R, relPinnedChart C R π b)
   106	      (Γ(relCurve C R, relPinnedChart C R π b) ⧸
   107	        Ideal.span {relThetaResSide a b (le_rfl) s}) :=
   108	  Submodule.map
   109	    (Ideal.Quotient.mkₐ Γ(relCurve C R, relPinnedChart C R π b)
   110	      (Ideal.span {relThetaResSide a b (le_rfl) s})).toLinearMap
   111	    (chartReadIdeal K b)
   112	
   113	/-- The ideal-theoretic colength module is exactly the previously defined `B`-span of the
   114	classes of the chart readings. -/
   115	theorem chartIdealColengthModule_eq_chartColengthModule
   116	    (K : Submodule R (relThetaSections C R π a)) (b : Bool)
   117	    (s : relThetaSections C R π a) :
   118	    chartIdealColengthModule K b s = chartColengthModule K b s := by
   119	  rw [chartIdealColengthModule, chartReadIdeal, Submodule.map_span, chartColengthModule]
   120	  congr 1
   121	  ext x
   122	  constructor
   123	  · rintro ⟨_, ⟨m, rfl⟩, rfl⟩
   124	    exact ⟨m, rfl⟩
   125	  · rintro ⟨m, rfl⟩
   126	    exact ⟨chartReadMap K b m, ⟨m, rfl⟩, rfl⟩
   127	
   128	/-- The scalar-extension presentation of the chart-reading ideal after quotienting by the
   129	chosen section. -/
   130	noncomputable def chartIdealColengthMap
   131	    (K : Submodule R (relThetaSections C R π a)) (b : Bool)
   132	    (s : relThetaSections C R π a) :
   133	    Γ(relCurve C R, relPinnedChart C R π b) ⊗[R] ↥K →ₗ[Γ(relCurve C R,
   134	      relPinnedChart C R π b)]
   135	      (Γ(relCurve C R, relPinnedChart C R π b) ⧸
   136	        Ideal.span {relThetaResSide a b (le_rfl) s}) :=
   137	  LinearMap.liftBaseChange Γ(relCurve C R, relPinnedChart C R π b)
   138	    ((Ideal.Quotient.mkₐ R (Ideal.span {relThetaResSide a b (le_rfl) s})).toLinearMap.comp
   139	      (chartReadMap K b))
   140	
   141	set_option maxHeartbeats 2400000 in
   142	set_option synthInstance.maxHeartbeats 800000 in
   143	/-- The range of the quotient scalar-extension map is the ideal-theoretic colength module. -/
   144	theorem range_chartIdealColengthMap
   145	    (K : Submodule R (relThetaSections C R π a)) (b : Bool)
   146	    (s : relThetaSections C R π a) :
   147	    LinearMap.range (chartIdealColengthMap K b s) = chartIdealColengthModule K b s := by
   148	  rw [chartIdealColengthModule_eq_chartColengthModule]
   149	  simpa only [chartIdealColengthMap, chartColengthModule] using
   150	    (LinearMap.range_liftBaseChange_eq_span
   151	      (R := R) (B := Γ(relCurve C R, relPinnedChart C R π b))
   152	      (M := ↥K)
   153	      (N := Γ(relCurve C R, relPinnedChart C R π b) ⧸
   154	        Ideal.span {relThetaResSide a b (le_rfl) s})
   155	      ((Ideal.Quotient.mkₐ R
   156	        (Ideal.span {relThetaResSide a b (le_rfl) s})).toLinearMap.comp
   157	          (chartReadMap K b)))
   158	
   159	end ThetaGeneratorSeed
   160	
   161	end AlgebraicGeometry
